chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no milk with which an infant is nursed that has greater blessing for it than the milk of its mother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a mother's milk in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise yet profound statement from Imam Ali (AS), linking the physical nourishment of the infant to spiritual *barakah*. This narration underscores the theological weight of maternal nursing, positioning it not merely as a biological necessity but as a sacred act that confers divine blessing, thereby reinforcing the legal and social primacy of the mother in early childhood care within Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the sanctity of the mother-child bond in the context of custody and upbringing.
